source.title: CONetV2: Efficient Auto-Channel Size Optimization for CNNs
source.authors: Yi-Ru Wang; Samir Khaki; Wei-Hang Zheng; M. S. Hosseini; K. Plataniotis

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that its Quality Condition metric correlates with generalization gap, using a different metric from the one in V7. The gap-correlation result is available only as a figure and a brief textual claim; it does not test the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports classification accuracy and parameter counts for channel-search methods, but those results do not report training error or train-test gaps. QC values used to guide channel search are not results about the generalization gap.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a channel-search method and a spectral Quality Condition metric. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test any other listed version. Its citation of generalization-measure research and its QC–gap correlation do not constitute a test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that QC, automated channel-dependency extraction, and weight transfer enable efficient channel search, with selected Greedy and Simulated Annealing configurations outperforming baselines. They report that Simulated Annealing generally offers better accuracy per parameter than Greedy; not every searched configuration beats its baseline.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a QC metric and channel-size search procedure; it does not reproduce the methods in the listed original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported QC gap-correlation result is shown for trained architectures from NATS-Bench; further conditions are not stated.

fits_no_version.finding: The Introduction asserts that QC correlates highly with test accuracy and generalization gap across trained NATS-Bench architectures; Figure 2 is cited, but numerical results are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A metric combining low-rank weight rank and spectral conditioning correlates with generalization gap across trained NATS-Bench architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
record.problems: The QC correlation with generalization gap is figure-only in the supplied text, without numerical values or uncertainty. The paper does not report train-test error gaps for its channel-search experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's channel-search accuracy and parameter-count comparisons are not rows because they do not measure training error, test error relative to training error, or a claim version's named behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error. Channel-search comparisons do not establish an interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under comparable tuning. Using different optimizers during search and final training is not this comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gap among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The omitted channel-search performance comparisons are declared in rows_left_out and do not establish any listed claim version. Improved accuracy with larger searched models alone does not test V2 without evidence about zero training error and the interpolation threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Whether widening beyond the interpolation threshold lowers test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected network generalization.
Large-batch effects on the train-test gap.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: trained architectures from the NATS-Bench
rows.operation_detail: The paper presents the Quality Condition metric's correlation with generalization gap.
rows.measure: Correlation between Quality Condition and generalization gap
rows.note: The text states that the metric has high correlation with generalization gap, but provides no correlation value. This is a different measure from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: QC combines low-rank weight rank and a spectral condition number; it does not measure tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations as V7 requires. The authors assert high correlation with generalization gap, but the supplied text contains no readable coefficient, direction, uncertainty, or plotted values. Retain only as a finding outside the listed versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
